## Publications

::: {.publication}
### Understanding Varieties of Religious Types: A Latent Profile Analysis of U.S. National Data

**Baker, A. W.**, Song, J., & Ryff, C. D. (2026). *Psychology of Religion and Spirituality*. Advance online publication.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1037/rel0000631){.btn .btn-sm .btn-primary} [OSF project](https://doi.org/10.17605/OSF.IO/YSD2C){.btn .btn-sm .btn-outline-dark}

**Overview.** Religion and spirituality are multidimensional, but they are often studied one dimension at a time. Using a person-centered approach and a national sample of U.S. adults, this study identifies distinct religion-and-spirituality profiles and examines how they differ across sociodemographic and psychological characteristics.
:::

Ryff, C. D., Cha, S. E., **Baker, A. W.**, & Song, J. (2025). *Psychology of Aesthetics, Creativity, and the Arts*. Advance online publication.

[Paper](https://doi.org/10.1037/aca0000805){.btn .btn-sm .btn-outline-dark}

## Current research

My current work examines the diversity, stability, and change of religious and spiritual life, as well as its connections with eudaimonic well-being. I am especially interested in the existential dimensions of religious experience—including meaning, purpose, transcendence, belonging, and doubt—and in the forms of heterogeneity that disappear when religion is reduced to a single belief, behavior, or score.

This work currently draws on large-scale longitudinal data and person-centered methods, including latent profile and latent transition analysis. Those tools are part of a broader methodological commitment rather than the boundary of the program: I want to develop creative, empirically rigorous ways of representing the complexity of lived experience and to let substantive questions guide the choice of data and method.
